key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of unseen metal-halide perovskites from accelerated ageing data, enabling faster stability screening.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable way to reduce experimental testing time for perovskite solar-cell materials while preserving interpretability of degradation drivers.
method: Collected 167 perovskite samples spanning compositions and crystallinities under heat and light stress
Featurized over 86,000 photoluminescence spectra with a physics-informed representation
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples and identify key stability descriptors
evidence_signal: The study uses a diverse dataset of 167 materials and more than 86k PL spectra, and reports that the model generalizes across material groups and outperforms baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Forecast quality may depend on the representativeness of the accelerated ageing conditions and the training set’s coverage of composition and crystallinity space.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
